key_insight: Photovoltaics can look highly energy-positive at the panel or fleet level, but their net energy drops sharply once continuous, reliable electricity delivery is required.
engineering_relevance: System designers must account for storage, overbuild, backup generation, and fuel supply, because firming constraints can erase much of the apparent EROI advantage and increase lifecycle emissions.
method: Boundary expansion from installation-level EROI to reliable electricity supply
Comparative scenarios: unfirmed renewables, battery firming, hydrogen firming, gas backup
evidence_signal: The abstract reports illustrative Central European benchmark ranges showing unfirmed EROI of 10.7–16.0, battery firming falling to 0.7–12.5 depending on duration, and gas backup reducing EROI to roughly 1.0–2.6 with higher GWP intensities.
watch_item: These are accounting benchmarks, not simulations or real-system predictions, and the results assume favorable reference settings that real deployments will likely worsen.
paper_title: Photovoltaics beyond the panel: system-level net energy under grid and firming constraints
